report.summary: One review_recommended finding: the profile response now returns tax ID and date of birth, PII that no information asset in app.tm.hcl classifies.

findings.title: Profile API now returns tax ID and date of birth with no matching information asset

model_excerpt.quote: information_asset "user credentials" classification=Restricted — Usernames and password hashes in the users table

evidence.note: profileResponse struct gains TaxID and DateOfBirth JSON fields
profileHandler now serializes u.TaxID and u.DateOfBirth into the GET /profile response body

relevance.justification: Tax ID and date of birth are personal data returned over an authenticated endpoint, and the model's only information asset covers credentials, so the new data is unclassified.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl for the login service threat model. The GET /profile response in internal/httpapi/user.go was changed in this PR to include two new personal-data fields: TaxID (json "tax_id") and DateOfBirth (json "date_of_birth") on profileResponse (lines ~11 and ~22). The model currently declares only one information_asset, "user credentials" (Usernames and password hashes in the users table, classification Restricted) at app.tm.hcl:7. Add a new information_asset block — e.g. information_asset "user pii" with description "Tax identification number and date of birth returned by GET /profile" and an appropriate classification (Restricted or Confidential per your scheme) — and update the description of threat "session hijacking" (app.tm.hcl:12) to note that a replayed session token now exposes this PII in addition to profile identity, so the Confidentiality impact reflects the wider blast radius.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an information_asset block for tax ID / date of birth PII and reference it in the session hijacking threat description.
